questions.prompt: What are the three pillars of observability?

options.text: Images, containers, and volumes
Logs, metrics, and traces
Build, test, and deploy
CPU, memory, and disk

questions.explanation: The three pillars are logs (events), metrics (numbers over time), and traces (a single request's path across services).

questions.prompt: Why prefer structured logging over free-form text?

options.text: It uses less disk always
Machine-readable records with consistent fields can be filtered, searched, and aggregated across many containers
It disables logging
It is required by Docker

questions.explanation: Structured logs (e.g. JSON with fields) let you query things like 'all status:500 on /orders in the last hour' and aggregate across services — hard with plain text.

options.text: Services push metrics to it over email
It uses a pull model, scraping each service's /metrics endpoint on a schedule
It reads them from the Dockerfile
It does not collect metrics

questions.explanation: Prometheus scrapes (pulls) a /metrics endpoint from each service on a schedule and stores the values as time series, often visualized in Grafana.

questions.prompt: A ______ probe decides whether to send a container traffic, while a liveness probe decides whether to restart it. (one word)
questions.explanation: A readiness probe controls whether traffic is sent; a liveness probe controls whether the container is restarted. They answer different questions.

questions.prompt: Which question is each observability pillar best at answering?

options.text: Logs say where, metrics say why, traces say if
Metrics say something is wrong, traces say where, logs say why
They all answer the same question
Metrics say why, logs say where, traces say nothing

questions.explanation: Metrics detect and trend a problem, traces localize where the time or failure is across services, and logs explain why it happened.

questions.prompt: Which are good observability practices? Select all that apply.

options.text: Alert on symptoms users feel, like error rate and latency (SLOs)
Emit structured logs to stdout and ship them to a central store
Implement distinct liveness and readiness probes
Rely on logs alone and skip metrics entirely

questions.explanation: Alert on user-facing symptoms, use structured logs, and separate liveness from readiness. Metrics are what you dashboard and alert on, so logs alone are not enough.
